title: process-bigraph interface manifest, version 1
description: The step and process classes an environment (an image, a conda or pixi env, a virtualenv) provides, with their configuration schemas and ports, as data. Types are bigraph-schema type expressions in their own string or dict forms, and addresses are process-bigraph addresses, exactly as the classes declare them, so any tool that reads bigraph-schema types can use a manifest: an editor or checker, a workbench, a registry, a prompt-driven authoring tool. Produced by running describe_env.py (process-bigraph-lang) inside the environment. Readers ignore keys they do not know, so producers may add more.

environment.description: Where the manifest was read: the environment, and the versions that shaped what was found.

name.description: The environment's name for whoever runs documents in it (a simulator name, a bundle).

image.description: The image reference it was read from, ideally pinned by digest.

packages.description: Distribution name to version, for the distributions providing the roots.

roots.description: The module roots whose submodules were imported.

errors.description: Modules or classes that could not be read; their components are missing.

type.description: A bigraph-schema type expression: the string form ('float', 'map[array[float]]', 'float{0.5}') or the dict form ({"_type": "float", "_default": 0.5}).

ports.description: Port name to type, as inputs() or outputs() returns them; null when they depend on an instance (see dynamic_ports).

kind.description: process (has an interval) or step; adapter is a step that converts between faces.

address.description: The process-bigraph address that instantiates it, e.g. local:!package.module.Class.

module.description: The module that defines the class.

description.description: The first paragraph of the class docstring.

config_schema.description: The class's config_schema as authored, key by key. A default is part of the type. A value that is not a type expression is null.

dynamic_ports.description: True when the ports depend on an instance (its config or its children), so inputs and outputs may be null or partial.
